narrative_profile: Third-person limited, locked to Elena March. Gothic psychological horror driven by slow-burn dread, atmospheric wrongness, and emotional recognition over shock. Every chapter carries an image of quiet wrongness. The prose is intimate but restrained, with heavy reliance on sensory detail, reflection imagery, and the unspoken.
surface_case: A grieving woman alone in a decaying inherited lake house, hunting for the reason her late aunt left it to her. Doors that were locked open at night. Footsteps cross the attic overhead when no one is there. A child's ghost watches from every reflective surface. On the surface it reads as a classic haunting — the house is holding something, and it wants her.
true_case: The girl in blue is not a ghost and not a stranger. She is the narrator's own eight-year-old self — the part she severed and left behind in this house the summer she was eight, in order to survive a single unbearable thing she did at the water's edge. The one-eyed bear is the vessel that holds that severed memory; whoever holds it begins to remember. The girl is not trying to harm her — she is trying to make her stay and become whole again, because being remembered means being reunited, and being reunited means the narrator must finally know, and own, what happened the day someone drowned. The haunting is not an attack. It is a part of herself asking to come home.
core_question: What did Elena do at the lake the summer she was eight that forced her to split herself and forget?
emotional_question: Can Elena face the truth of her past, reclaim the part of herself she abandoned, and live with the guilt, or will she choose to remain safely fractured?
book1_promise: The central mystery will be fully solved: the reader will learn exactly what happened to Tomas and why Elena's memory is missing. Elena's emotional arc will resolve through a choice at the water's edge. The story will deliver concrete partial answers every 2-3 chapters, rewarding reader investment, and end with a complete emotional and narrative closure for the main question.
book2_hook: In Cora's final diary entry, Elena finds proof her aunt did the exact same thing decades earlier — split herself, hid a bear, left a child in the dark. But Cora's second shadow was never taken back. It is still in the house. And now that Elena is whole, it has started appearing in her reflection, wearing Cora's face.
book1_ending_type: Central mystery fully solved; protagonist's arc resolves with reintegration and acceptance of guilt. A new series-level mystery is seeded via the discovery of Cora's parallel story, setting up a direct sequel.
reader_payoff_book1: The gratification of a carefully constructed psychological mystery that pays off every planted clue; the catharsis of Elena's emotional reintegration and the poignant horror of realizing the ghost was herself; a complete, satisfying narrative that can stand alone while unmistakably setting up a larger series.
